chunks: ʿAmr ibn Shimr narrated from Jābir, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله underwent cupping. A mawlā of Banī Bayāḍah cupped him, and he gave him payment. Had it been haram, he would not have given him payment.
When he had finished, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to him: “Where is the blood?” He said: “I drank it, O Messenger of Allah.”
So he said: “It was not appropriate for you to do that, and Allah has made it a barrier for you from the Fire.”

key_terms.مَوْلًى: a client or servant associated with a tribe

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to take payment for cupping in Shia hadith, and what did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله say about drinking the cupped blood?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله paid the cupper for his work, indicating the permissibility of taking wages for cupping. It also recounts that the cupper drank the blood, which the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله disapproved of, while informing him that Allah had made it a protection for him from the Fire.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3585 - Imam Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), narrated through Jabir from Amr ibn Shimr:

"The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, underwent cupping. A servant from the tribe of Banu Bayadah performed the cupping, and the Prophet (sw) gave him payment. If it were prohibited, he would not have given him payment.

When the procedure was completed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, asked him: 'Where is the blood?'
The servant replied: 'I drank it, O Messenger of Allah (swt).'
The Prophet said: 'You should not have done that, but Allah (swt) has made it a barrier for you against the Fire.'"
